note: 170+ wildlife species across Leonida's 6 regions (including 62 bird species).

items.name: Alligator
items.notes: Common in Grassrivers swamps, waterways, and muddy banks. Lethal ambush bite in shallow water.

items.name: Florida Panther / Cougar
items.notes: Stalks dense pine trails and ridges in Mount Kalaga National Park, especially at dusk and night.

items.name: Black Bear
items.notes: Roams Mount Kalaga forests and riverbanks; charges if provoked or cornered.

items.name: Bobcat
items.notes: Agile wildcat spotted in rocky brush across Mount Kalaga and rural Ambrosia.

items.name: Whitetail Buck
items.notes: Antlered male deer grazing in Mount Kalaga meadows; flees quickly when spooked.

items.name: Whitetail Doe
items.notes: Found in small herds alongside Whitetail Bucks in northern Leonida.

items.name: Wild Boar
items.notes: Spotted across Mount Kalaga National Park & Leonida Keys brush; can charge on foot.

items.name: Nine-Banded Armadillo
items.notes: Forages along dirt roadsides and rural scrub in Port Gellhorn and Ambrosia.

items.name: White River Otter
items.notes: Playful wetland mammal found along Grassrivers creeks and clear marsh banks.

items.name: Rhesus Macaque
items.notes: Invasive primate troops living in Leonida's wooded wetlands and river islands.

items.name: Green Iguana
items.notes: Sunbathes on seawalls, docks, and palm trunks throughout the Leonida Keys.

items.name: Cane Toad
items.notes: Nocturnal amphibian found in damp grass, canals, and suburban lawns after rain.

items.name: Raccoon
items.notes: Scavenges alley dumpsters and motel fringes at night across Port Gellhorn & Vice City.

items.name: Red Fox
items.notes: Spotted darting across forest clearings at dawn and dusk.

items.name: Beaver
items.notes: Builds lodges along Mount Kalaga streams and northern river bends.

items.name: Skunk
items.notes: Nocturnal forager around rural Ambrosia farms and roadside brush.

items.name: Squirrel
items.notes: Common in city parks, palm trees, and wooded trails across Leonida.

items.name: Snake
items.notes: Slithers through tall marsh grass and rocky ledges in Grassrivers and Mount Kalaga.

items.name: American Flamingo
items.notes: Iconic bright-pink wading flocks in Leonida Keys flats and Grassrivers wetlands.

items.name: Pelican
items.notes: Perches on marina pilings and dives for fish along Vice Beach and the Keys.

items.name: Great Blue Heron
items.notes: Tall coastal wading bird stalking shallow marshes and canals.

items.name: Osprey
items.notes: Fish-hunting raptor nesting on channel markers and coastal towers.

items.name: Roseate Spoonbill
items.notes: Distinctive pink marsh bird sweeping shallow Grassrivers lagoons.

items.name: Whooping Crane
items.notes: Rare tall white wetland crane spotted in open Grassrivers flats.

items.name: Double-Crested Cormorant
items.notes: Diving waterbird frequently seen drying its wings on docks and buoys.

items.name: Duck
items.notes: Common across ponds, canals, and calm wetland coves.

items.name: Seagull
items.notes: Flocks over Vice Beach boardwalks, piers, and marinas.

items.name: Bald Eagle
items.notes: Soars high above Mount Kalaga peaks and northern lakes.

items.name: Woodpecker
items.notes: Heard drumming on pine trunks throughout Mount Kalaga National Park.

items.name: Pigeon
items.notes: Ubiquitous across Vice City sidewalks, plazas, and rooftops.

items.name: Manatee
items.notes: Gentle marine mammal gliding through warm Keys coves and coastal springs.

items.name: Hammerhead Shark
items.notes: Patrols deeper reefs and offshore channels around the Leonida Keys.

items.name: Great White Shark
items.notes: Deep offshore waters beyond the Vice City coastline—lethal to unprotected swimmers.

items.name: Dolphin
items.notes: Pods leap alongside boats in Vice Bay and the Leonida Keys.

items.name: Sea Turtle
items.notes: Swims around coral reefs and shipwreck dive spots in the Keys.

items.name: Stingray / Manta Ray
items.notes: Glides over sandy shoals and shallow turquoise reefs.

items.name: Lionfish
items.notes: Striped invasive reef fish hovering near sunken wrecks and coral ledges.

items.name: Killer Whale
items.notes: Rare deep-ocean sighting far offshore beyond the continental drop-off.

items.name: Eel
items.notes: Hides inside reef crevices and underwater wrecks.

items.name: Jellyfish
items.notes: Drifts in coastal currents off Vice Beach and Keys reefs.

items.name: Crayfish
items.notes: Freshwater crustacean found in muddy Grassrivers creeks and bayous.

items.name: Australian Shepherd
items.notes: Friendly herding dog seen on beaches and suburban parks.

items.name: Chihuahua
items.notes: Common along Ocean Beach walkways and boutique sidewalks.

items.name: Doberman
items.notes: Sleek guard breed spotted near upscale Vice City estates and yards.

items.name: German Shepherd
items.notes: Loyal working dog seen with locals across Port Gellhorn and Ambrosia.

items.name: Labrador Retriever
items.notes: Friendly retriever frequently spotted on docks and Keys beaches.

items.name: Rottweiler
items.notes: Heavy-set breed seen around industrial yards and residential porches.

items.name: Poodle
items.notes: Walked along luxury Vice City shopping avenues and resorts.

items.name: Domestic Cat
items.notes: Lounges on alley steps, porches, and Key Lento docks; can be petted.
